question: to the Commission Maria Zacharia (NI) Subject:
Israel’s expulsion of Greek trade union delegation and criteria for reviewing compliance with Article 2 of the EU-Israel Association Agreement

On 21 June 2026, the Israeli authorities refused entry to and expelled a Greek trade union delegation travelling to Ramallah at the invitation of Palestinian organisations. The incident prompted the Greek Ministry of Foreign Affairs to make a formal complaint. This adds to a series of complaints concerning restrictions against members of civil society, yet the Commission is still not recommending activating the clause in Article 2 of the EUIsrael Association Agreement, despite acknowledging that this Article – which provides that relations between the parties must be based on respect for human rights and democratic principles – constitutes an essential element of the Agreement. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.

What specific legal, factual and institutional criteria does it apply to assess compliance with Article 2 of the EU-Israel Association Agreement and to determine the conditions for activating the relevant clause?
Are these criteria included in internal opinions, compliance assessments or other Commission documents and, if so, why are they not made public and communicated to the European Parliament?

Does it consider that the expulsion of an EU Member State’s citizens on account of their trade union and political activity is an element that is taken into account when assessing compliance with Article 2 and, if not, why not?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (3.8.2026) The High Representative/Vice-President conducted – with the support of a majority of Member States – a review of Israel’s compliance with its obligations under Article 2 of the EU-Israel Association Agreement1 in May 2025. The review concluded that there are indications that Israel would be in breach of its obligations. Discussions continue in the Council on the package of measures presented by the Commission following the review. Suspension of the entire agreement would require unanimity of all 27 Member States. The assessment was carried out by the European External Action Service, in coordination with the services of the Commission, relying in particular on factual reports by relevant international and United Nations organisations.
